shower.thought: We're all just trying to be the person someone believes we are.
You've never actually seen your own face, only reflections and photographs of it.
The moment you learn something new, you become a different person than you were seconds ago, but you're the only one who knows it.
Nostalgia is just grief for a time period instead of a person.
You can't remember being born, so there's technically a part of your life you experienced but have zero access to.
The things you worry about the most are usually things you have the least control over.
Every conversation you have is a collaboration between two different realities of what just happened.
You're statistically more likely to be alive right now than at any other point in human history.
Phones have made us all simultaneously more connected and more alone.
The only time you're truly on time is when you're late by accident.
We keep receipts for things we buy, but never for moments we experience.
Your sense of humor is just your coping mechanism on display.
The scariest part of aging isn't looking different—it's realizing that everyone else is aging too.
If aliens exist, they're probably also wondering if they're alone in the universe.
You've probably had conversations that changed someone's life without ever knowing it.
The people you'll never meet have shaped your entire life.
Forgetting is just remembering in reverse, which means memory isn't as reliable as we pretend.
You spend so much time preparing for the future that the present becomes the past before you notice.
Distance doesn't make people grow apart—attention does.
Boredom might just be your brain asking for something it actually needs.

darkjoke.thought:
My grandfather said, "Life is like a box of chocolates."
I said, "You mean you never know what you're gonna get?" He said, "No, I mean eventually you get to the bottom and feel empty inside."

I tried to join a gym, but they said I had to commit for a year.
I said, "I'm already in a relationship where nobody's happy. I don't need another."

My friend asked why I stopped going to church.
I said, "It's hard to feel spiritual when you realize the only difference between prayer and talking to yourself is one of them people judge you less for doing in public."

I told my dad I wanted to write a book about my life.
He said, "Honey, your life isn't a book. It's a tweet with a lot of typos."

The doctor told me I had six months to live.
I couldn't pay the bill, so he gave me another six months.

My therapist asked what my biggest fear was.
I said, "Turning into my parents." She said, "That ship has sailed."
I said, "When?" She said, "Years ago. You didn't notice because you were too busy doing their exact voice."

I asked my friend why she unfollowed me on Instagram.
She said, "Because every time I see your posts, I remember you exist, and my day gets worse."

They say money can't buy happiness.
But it can buy a jet ski. Have you ever seen someone frowning on a jet ski?
You will. That's my uncle. He's just realized he still has to go home.

I went to a self-help seminar called "Finding Your Purpose."
The presenter asked, "Who here feels lost?" Everyone raised their hand.
He said, "Great, you've found it. That'll be $200."

My kid asked if there's life after death.
I said, "I don't know, but based on how I feel after work, probably not."

I asked my Alexa if I was going to die alone.
She said, "I can't answer that, but would you like me to order more cat food?"

My accountant said I should think about my financial future.
I told him, "I'm trying not to think about any future."

I saw my ex at the grocery store and hid behind the cereal boxes.
She found me anyway. Turns out she was doing the same thing from the other side.

They say "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger."
Tell that to my immune system. It's had every virus known to man and it's never been more pathetic.

I told my boss I'd work from home to be more productive.
He said, "That's great." I've been unemployed for three months now.
Turns out "work from home" was corporate speak for "we're firing you, but slowly."

My friend told me he was becoming a vegan for ethical reasons.
I asked how he got so moral. He said, "Turns out it's easy to be ethical when you're also being insufferable."

I went to a fortune teller.
She said I'd live a long life. I said, "Is that good or bad news?"
She charged me extra not to answer.

My doctor said I need to cut back on alcohol.
I asked, "Will I live longer?"
He said, "No, it'll just feel longer."

I told my wife she was cold.
She said, "No, I'm just distant."
I said, "Those are the same thing." She said, "Exactly."

My therapist asked if I ever feel like giving up.
I said, "Every day." She said, "Same."
I said, "Wait, are you my therapist or am I yours?" She said, "That'll be $150."
